recipes.name: Ham and Cheese Crescent Roll-Ups
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can Pillsbury® Refrigerated Crescent Dinner Rolls
4 thin slices Cheddar cheese, cut into strips

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Separate crescent dough into 8 triangles on a flat work surface. Place 1 slice ham on each triangle; place 2 cheese strips down center of ham. Fold in edges of ham to match dough triangle shape.
Roll up each crescent roll, starting at wide end, ending at triangle tip. Place rolls, tips down, on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 15 to 19 minutes. Remove from cookie sheet immediately; serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Cheese Crescent Roll-Ups
raw_recipe.description: This ham and cheese crescent roll-up recipe requires just 3-simple ingredients, making them a quick and easy meal that both kids and adults will love.

review.reviewBody: I made this as a quick lunch for the boys. I used swiss only because that was what I had on hand. My crescent rolls were also reduced fat. I made a homemade honey-mustard dressing to go with. They made quick work of these roll-up's--they were gone in less than ten minutes. Next time, I'll double the recipe.

Easy lunch, dinner, appetizer; husband loved them. I made half of them with cheddar and the other half with Swiss cheese, equally good. Made this variation which turned out very well. I had some leftover baked Italian chicken breast (boneless) and angel hair pasta with sauce. I chopped the chicken, put chicken, parmesan cheese, and a small spoonful of marinara sauce on each Crescent triangle, rolled up as for the ham and cheese roll-ups. Baked at 350 for about 15-18 minutes. Served with marinara for dipping and left-over pasta. Made an excellent lunch.

Nice concept and very versatile. A single triangle wrap would be way too small a serving in my house; therefore, I put 2 triangles of dough together to form a rectangle, being careful to join all seams ( one tube of crescent rolls will make 4 crescent wraps). I covered the rectangle with a thin layer of light honey mustard dressing. After this, I chopped a large slice of ham, folded it into one slice of Swiss, basically folding the slice in half to act as a "pocket" for the cheese. I placed the pocket into the "sauced" rectangle. I wrapped the dough around the cheese/ham pocket, joining the long sides together & closing all seams by pinching with my fingers tips. I then folded the short ends in toward the center (similar to wrapping a present) and closed all seams. Cooked for 13 minutes, then turned the wraps over & cooked for an additional 5 minutes. It made a nice presentation (similar to hot pockets), but was greasy (that's why I'm giving only 4 stars). Next time I will make these using pizza dough instead of crescent rolls to reduce fat. This recipe has a lot of potential!

Tasty. Not a big crescent roll fan but I had some left over from the holiday season, so tried this as a breakfast idea for my teen. I had small slices of ham (about the size of Canadian bacon) so I used two for each, folded in half, and one slice of cheddar torn in strips, some under and some over the ham. Sprinkled with chives and spread some Dijon mustard on the cheese, as I knew they would be very buttery and maybe need something to perk them up. Also baked these a few extra minutes to ensure they were not too soft. I liked them, will see what the teen thinks!

Super easy, and really tasty! I was surprised how filling these are. A tad bit on the greasy side. Not sure if that's because I used bricked cheddar or not. The only thing I did differently was add mustard before I rolled them. It adds a nice flavour. I will be making these again for sure! Great recipe!!

Easy lunch/meal for kids. Just add a fruit or veggie on the side. I've made these twice using ham & american cheese and ham & cheddar cheese. These are very versatile since you could use any meat/cheese combination you wanted. Cook on one of the top racks of your oven or the bottoms will get burned. Also go light on the cheese or it will melt out of the crescents and make a mess on your baking sheet.

I doubled the recipe because we were having these for dinner with soup on the side. We all liked them quite a bit, but I felt they needed a little "something", so I dipped mine in mustard. They were a little difficult to roll up with the sliced cheddar cheese, so I think next time I'll try using shredded cheese instead. I think they'd also be phenomenal brushed with a little garlic butter as soon as they come put of the oven.

Will absolutely make again. So easy. I used a half slice of ham and a half slice of packaged cheddar cheese slices. I didn't even tuck the ham in. Rolled up nicely and baked for 17 minutes total. Served with dijon mustard for dipping. Huge hit at my house.
These are delicious, family loved them. I used sharp cheddar on half and Swiss on the other half. I used Dijon mustard. Thanks for a fun meal.
I did half with cheddar and half with pepper jack... Brushed the tops with honey butter and they're a hit!

These are delicious; great for a quick weekend lunch. We've make them with ham & cheddar, but our favorite way to make them is with pepperoni & string cheese, served w/ marinara on the side for dipping (3-4 pepperonis & half a stick of string cheese per roll).
great meal l add green beans and so good a total keeper!

Delicious, easy and quick. I substituted provolone and Swiss and both work every bit as well as the cheddar. I used spiral sliced ham and topped the rolls with butter spray for a little extra flavor 😋 This is a great dish when you're pressed for time
My husband loved these as a breakfast treat. Thanks a bunch
Great with honey mustard, great without
Easy to do, great lunch or quick dinner. I used several different cheeses, Provolone,Swiss, Gouda, and good ol American. something for everyone.
It was pretty easy, but the kids weren’t really impressed.... though my older one is super picky but the husband liked it.
Easy enough to make that my five year old helped!
Very good appetizer
These were good. Kind of like homemade hotpockets. The kids loved them.
